audit.whatIsWrong: content win[4] gives Level 6 to Swain and win[5] calls First item even, but whys[4] says 'your R heal-amp dive beats him before his R sustain ramps' and whys[5] says 'your bruiser spike out-brawls his squishy poke build'. The spikes and the mid prose agree with the whys, not with the chart. The packet chart is Aatrox through First item.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a 120s drain that needs soul stacks and bodies to be worth anything; at level 6 with no stacks it loses to World Ender's heal amp. 53.18% over 1794 games.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and First item both read Aatrox; Two+ items stays Swain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike talks about 'his E cooldown' without ever giving it, and Demonic Ascension is described as a sustain ramp with no duration or cooldown.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 and Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s. Death's Hand is 7s at rank 1, which is why his chip feels constant.
audit.corrected: 12s Nevermove, 7s Death's Hand and 120s Demonic Ascension written into the spikes and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says 'dodge his E Nevermove root' six different ways without once stating HOW. Nevermove does not root on the way out — the wave travels forward, returns to Swain, and roots on the return. It also never mentions that Death's Hand does more damage the more bolts hit you, which means it is at its strongest in melee, exactly where Aatrox wants to be.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer.' and 'Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by.' Walking through the outgoing wave is free; standing on the line it comes home on is what gets you rooted and pulled. That single fact is the difference between dodging Nevermove and guessing at it.
audit.corrected: Return-trip root and the pull follow-up stated in spikes[0], mid and wants.foe[0]; the point-blank Death's Hand penalty stated in mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says Grievous Wounds is needed, despite the whole late-game section being about him out-healing you.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him off Soul Fragments and permanently raises his maximum health, and Demonic Ascension drains from every nearby champion, minion and monster. Anti-heal is the item that decides the extended fight the entry keeps describing.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in spikes[1].text alongside the 120s R.

edits.before: Your window: once you have the Q pattern, dodge his E Nevermove root and gap-close with Umbral Dash, then land Q3 sweetspot into W and drain — with his E down his short poke can't out-trade you.
edits.after: Your window: Nevermove roots on its return, not on the way out — walk through the outgoing wave, then leave the line it comes home on. Umbral Dash in, Q3 sweetspot, drain: 12s E down, he has no answer.

edits.before: R World Ender heal-amp lets you dive through his zone and drain-brawl him before his R Demonic Ascension sustain ramps; commit while his E is on cooldown and you win the all-in.
edits.after: World Ender's heal amp beats Demonic Ascension (120s), which drains off you and the wave — bring Grievous Wounds and commit in the 12s after Nevermove, not into a soul stack.

edits.before: The mid game stays yours. Swain's E root sets up everything — dodge it and he's just a mage with no follow-up, so bait or sidestep it, then gap-close with Umbral Dash, land Q3 into W, and drain. At 6 your R World Ender heal amp lets you dive through his zone and win the brawl before his R Demonic Ascension sustain ramps; commit while his E is down and your drain out-heals his chip. His first-item poke stings, but your bruiser spike still out-brawls him up close.
edits.after: The mid game stays yours. Nevermove sets up everything and it roots on the return trip: let the outgoing wave pass, then step off the line it comes home on, and he is a mage with no follow-up. Death's Hand hits hardest point-blank, every bolt landing at once, so burst and step out instead of standing on him. At 6 dive through the zone on World Ender before his 120s Demonic Ascension stacks souls, committing in the 12s his E is down.

edits.before: Land E root into full Q poke barrage
edits.after: Root you on Nevermove's return trip

edits.before: Swain changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Swain E pull and R drain. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Swain wants to keep distance, poke Aatrox before he can reach the wave, and punish missed Qs with ranged damage or crowd control.
edits.after: Swain changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Nevermove (E, 12s), which roots on its return trip and then drags him in. Aatrox wins by letting the outgoing wave pass, stepping off the line it comes home on, and spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings. Swain wants distance, Death's Hand chip every 7s, and a soul-stacked Demonic Ascension that out-heals the drain.
